description:
gh-70. On an incrementally-updated PDF (/Prev chain, e.g. Okular annotation save), rasterizing a page before resolving objects makes later resolve() return the OLD pre-update object. Page /Annots resolves 3 entries instead of 8.

Root cause: mupdf/xref.rs load_obj_stm() caches EVERY object it parses out of an object stream (self.cache.entry(onum).or_insert(cached)) without checking the xref actually says that object number lives in THIS object stream. On an incremental update the superseded object still physically sits in the old objstm; rasterize touches some other object in that same objstm, the whole stream gets decompressed, and the stale copy lands in the cache first-write-wins. Every later resolve() of that num is served the stale copy.

Upstream MuPDF guards exactly this in pdf_load_obj_stm (source/pdf/pdf-xref.c:2213): it only stores the parsed object when (entry->type == 'o' || entry->type == 'O') && entry->ofs == num -- i.e. the xref must claim that object for this very stream -- and pdf_drop_obj()s it otherwise. Our port dropped that guard.

Fix: port the guard, plus a regression test with an incremental update superseding an objstm object.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
FIXED. Ported MuPDF's guard from pdf_load_obj_stm (pdf-xref.c:2213) as PdfDocument::claimed_by_objstm(): an object parsed out of object stream S is only cached when the xref still says XrefEntry::Compressed{stm_num: S}. Objects the newest xref section has superseded (now 'n' at a fresh offset) are skipped before parsing, so they can never reach the first-write-wins cache.

Regression test mupdf::xref::tests::incremental_update_supersedes_object_stream_copy + fixture incremental_update_pdf(): original body packs objs 1/2/3 into objstm 4 (xref stream 5); appended update supersedes obj 3 uncompressed with MediaBox 400 + /Annots of 5, indexed by xref stream 6 via /Prev + /Index [3 1 6 1]. Verified the test FAILS without the guard (MediaBox 200 not 400 -- same shape as the reported 3-vs-8 /Annots) and passes with it.

Gates: cargo test --release -p kopitiam-pdf = 329+1+2 pass; all 8 reverse-dep crates pass; cargo clippy --release --all-targets clean for xref.rs (4 warnings all pre-existing in doc_stream/font/page_image/stream.rs). Journal: docs/engineering-journal/2026-08-25-dropped-guards-in-a-port.md

title: kopitiam-pdf: load_obj_stm poisons the cache with superseded objects from an old object stream
